question: Does neuronal WWOX restoration started AFTER symptom onset recover any endpoint, or only prevent one when given in the neonatal window?
why_now: Every partial-benefit lever in this module is ordered as a bridge to, or a substitute for, restoration; whether restoration works after onset decides which of those two framings is the real one, so one result re-reads the whole list.
evidence_available: WWOX-system, read beyond the abstract: the high-dose arm reaches a survival plateau to day 300 and lowers spike-wave discharges to a wild-type-indistinguishable level; weight is ordered against wild type and the untreated knockout (equal to the high dose at P30 only), and glycaemia is NOT shown to be prevented: at P10 the treated arms are not significantly different from the untreated knockout (high dose about 113, low dose about 105, untreated knockout about 95; Figure 3E, card C04 DR-AAV-GLU10-HD and DR-AAV-GLU10-LD), at P20 the untreated-knockout comparator is absent because those animals are dead (Figure 3F, DR-AAV-GLU20-LD and DR-AAV-GLU20-HD, direction UNKNOWN) and the P20 result is dose-graded against wild type only, and by P30 the dose separation has closed (Figure 3G); the paper's own text states that both doses partially corrected hypoglycaemia, while the panel does not support it (card C04 records this: the treated arms are not significantly different from the untreated knockout at P10); the glucose result depends on age, dose and comparison, and a non-significant difference at P10 is not evidence of no benefit. Every treated arm was injected in the stated neonatal window.
decisive_uncertainty: No arm exists in which treatment begins after the phenotype is established; the window is stated, not measured against a later start, and P300 readouts are survivor-selected.
next_test: One added arm of the published design with injection after the first recorded spike-wave discharge, same endpoints, untreated same-genotype comparator kept. Worded per endpoint class: measure the restoration actually achieved at the age of treatment and its regional distribution, because the one comparable later-age failure in a short-lived null was left uninterpretable by that missing measurement; carry a within-animal pre-treatment recording, a treated wild-type or heterozygote arm, growth and glycaemia as primary endpoints (growth failed even with pre-onset treatment in the closest analogue), and follow-up long enough to see decay. Quantified myelin sheath structure (g-ratio or electron microscopy, not marker intensity) is the discriminating endpoint for a neuron-driven lesion: white-matter abnormality has been reversed after a documented onset only in glial or metabolic lesions, and sheath structure after onset has been reported only in a metabolic oligodendrocyte-enzyme lesion (G-ratio by electron microscopy, one source) and not in any neuron-driven lesion. Spike-wave rate is the confirmatory endpoint and its external precedent (not WWOX evidence) is split, so pair it with a rhythm or power-spectrum measure; interneuron number as well as excitability, because no source measured number.
feasibility: Established model and established vector; the added arm is a timing change, not a new assay.
novelty_perimeter: Queried: the two gene-addition cards (C01, C04) and their assertion rows; the deepdive manifest of the source; the work-order statements for this need. Checked for a post-onset arm and found none. Not a statement about the literature beyond the sources this module has read. Extended on 2026-11-05/06 by two bounded external searches (batch_sci_20261105, r1 and r2 query logs, 66 queries in all): conditional, antisense and vector restoration after onset in Mecp2, Ube3a, Fmr1, Tsc1, Pten, Syngap1, Cdkl5, Shank3, Tcf4, Scn1a, Scn1b, Kcnt1, Scn8a and leukodystrophy models. The earlier of the two searches was anchored on gene names and could not reach enzyme, connexin, tubulin or astrocyte-transporter leukodystrophies; an independent review found post-onset white-matter arms there. Bounded searches, not a statement that none exists.
origin_detail: Named in the WWOX literature and carded: the neonatal AAV9 gene-addition study (cards C01 and C04).
movement_note: No IT21 input changes the position. The row text was corrected in IT21 P1 (glycaemia is not called prevented).

question: Before any ISR-attenuating compound can be ordered: in a WWOX-deficient HUMAN neural system, does the ISR run high or low?
why_now: The need's direction is unresolved and the two available readouts disagree by design, so no compound on this axis can be qualified either way. Resolving the sign is the cheapest act that converts the largest blocked slice of the catalogue into an orderable or a refused question; leaving it unresolved keeps that slice invisible rather than negative.
evidence_available: WWOX-system transcript-level only and contradictory: the knockout organoid shows the ISR target set lower, one shRNA library per arm shows it higher, and the designs are not comparable. No ATF4 protein and no eIF2-alpha phosphorylation measurement exists in the sources read.
decisive_uncertainty: Which sign the ISR actually has at protein level in a WWOX-deficient human neural cell, and in which cell type. The IT28 reading of the transferable literature adds that the sign of a lever depends on which node is perturbed and on the stress class (chronic misfolded cargo versus a locked eIF2B lesion versus transient external stress), and that RNA target sets can disagree with eIF2-alpha phosphorylation in both directions. Until the protein-level sign is measured, an ISR-attenuating and an ISR-potentiating compound remain equally defensible.
next_test: ATF4 protein, total and phosphorylated eIF2-alpha and per-cell translation (nascent-protein labelling) in a WWOX-deficient human neural line against an isogenic control, at one differentiation stage and by cell type, no compound involved. Only if the sign is high, a pre-registered panel: an eIF2B activator and kinase-level loss against genetic PPP1R15A loss, with a second-stressor arm and a functional endpoint. IT30 (design hypothesis only, from the residues of CH-IT28-ISR-ROLE read in wo06_it30_20261106 and independently checked): keep a network-activity or seizure-relevant readout beside the protein-level sign; if a potentiation arm is tried, make it genetic (a PPP1R15B knockdown) or chemical with measured p-eIF2alpha and an alpha-2 control (guanabenz acts on alpha-2 receptors and Sephin1 and guanabenz were not shown to inhibit PPP1R15A-PP1); the only mammalian seizure-endpoint precedent for a potentiator is two studies of one eIF2-alpha phosphatase inhibitor with opposite signs, so no arm is promoted.
feasibility: A protein measurement on material the module already reasons about; no new model and no compound needed.
novelty_perimeter: Queried: this need's eleven observation rows and their readout levels; the ISR card and its assertions; the search layer over the eight ISR targets (78 associations, 56 families, none direction-coherent because the need direction is unresolved). The gap is a missing measurement in the sources this module has read, not a claim about the ISR literature.

intervention: T-type calcium blockade, proposed isoform-reach set to verify (efonidipine, flunarizine, against the carded T-type agents)
question: Which T-type isoform carries the suppression of the provoked seizure phase, and does the effect depend on the genotype?
why_now: The module's one T-type result is complex-or-group level with no isoform datum and no drug-by-genotype interaction test, and its own need file names both gaps. Two approved compounds are proposed as a pair that MAY differ in isoform reach; the pair is a proposal to verify, not a documented discriminating pair: the catalogue difference between them (one T-type target row for the first agent, three for the second) comes from annotation completeness, not from a documented functional selectivity, because in the catalogue both are tagged selectivity Not Determined and no fitted potency on the three isoforms is carried for the first agent (ChEMBL holds no calcium-channel activity for it), while the second has Kd values on all three only from synthesis papers that used it as a reference, in different assays and conditions. Absence of a subtype in a catalogue is not inactivity. Both agents also act on other targets (L-type channels for one, receptors beyond the channel family for the other), so the potency measures in one assay and species, at the concentration reached in the animal, are the first step.
evidence_available: WWOX-system: a T-type blocker suppressed the late phase of the provoked seizure score in the null mouse, one experiment, genotype specificity not established by an interaction. Catalogue: direction-coherent blocker actions on CACNA1G, CACNA1H and CACNA1I, at group and single-protein level, from curated mechanism rows.
decisive_uncertainty: Whether the carded effect is a T-type effect at all, which isoform carries it, and whether it is genotype-dependent. Whether the two agents really differ in isoform reach at the concentrations used is itself unmeasured. The same effect from two compounds is compatible with a common target (the T-type class) and does not by itself weaken the T-type attribution; it only fails to discriminate isoforms. What would weaken the attribution is no effect of either agent at on-target exposure, an effect that tracks off-target activity rather than T-type potency, or an equal effect in wild type (no genotype dependence).
next_test: The published provoked-seizure design with a drug-by-genotype interaction term and the proposed pair beside the carded agent, after the potency of each agent on the three isoforms has been qualified in one assay and species; identical provocation and scoring.
feasibility: Published assay, approved compounds, three arms added to an existing design.
novelty_perimeter: Queried: the search layer over CACNA1G, CACNA1H and CACNA1I (190 associations, 66 families); the T-type card and the ethosuximide and apinocaltamide units; the uncarded-items table; the IT9 to IT11 qualification records; a name scan of every card and ranking table for each proposed compound. Both proposals are absent from that WWOX material and are members of a class the module already holds, so this is a proposed probe set to verify, not a new biological relation.

question: Is there an axonal signal left for a pro-myelinating agent to act on, before any such agent is ordered?

The premise question is cheaper than any compound test and decides whether the axis is a target or a consequence.
evidence_available: WWOX-system: the myelin deficit is partly prevented when WWOX is restored in neurons in the neonatal window; the treated arms of the source are unquantified, and whether an established deficit re-myelinates is unmeasured. intervention: Agonist probe for the receptors of thyroid hormone (tiratricol, with liothyronine as comparator)
question: In a seizure-free neuron plus oligodendrocyte-precursor co-culture, does an agonist of the receptors for thyroid hormone release the maturation block seen after neuronal WWOX loss, and does it do so only in the WWOX-deficient condition?
why_now: It is the role-resolving question the glia and myelin work left open (IT14): the maturation block is receptor-responsive or it is not, and one co-culture answers that before any in vivo question is asked. It enters at rank 6, below the ten-row line and behind the lithium and GABA-T rows (which carry a risk flag and human clinical reports and are not displaced by conditional probes), because the test is cell-level and inexpensive and an approved molecule exists for any later step, not because it is new: the precedent comes from a hormone-uptake defect in another disease and does not transfer by itself, and it sits below the two premise measurements (the dichloroacetate and NRF2 rows).
evidence_available: WWOX-system: precursor cells increased and mature oligodendrocytes decreased after neuron-restricted WWOX deletion, restored by neuronal add-back (IT14), with the add-back window early; the myelin deficit is partly prevented when WWOX is restored in neurons in the neonatal window. Outside WWOX: in a mouse model of a thyroid-hormone-uptake defect, a thyromimetic normalised myelination and interneuron differentiation only when started in the first three postnatal weeks (abstract-level reading). No myelin compound has been given to a WWOX system, and another myelin compound already has a negative developmental-myelination result in this module. IT22 P6 (partial full text of the two human trials of the molecule in a hormone-entry defect; mouse rescue; OPC literature at abstract level): the human precedent has no neurodevelopmental endpoint; the mouse rescue works only in postnatal weeks 1-3 and the effective dose suppressed the thyroid axis; precursor cells express receptor-alpha rather than receptor-beta in rodents (abstract level), so a receptor-beta-leaning liver-directed agent is an isoform control, not a candidate; seizure evidence is mixed (worsening in 3 patients with prior seizures; hyperthyroid rats more seizure-prone).
decisive_uncertainty: Whether the block is receptor-responsive and causal, or a consequence of seizures, or of the neuron's own signal being absent (the pro-myelinating-class row asks the premise from the signal side). The agent also has systemic actions that oppose the glycaemia need; an effect on seizure threshold was not looked up. IT22: the seizure-threshold question is now looked up and is mixed, not closed.
next_test: Seizure-free neuron plus precursor co-culture with wild-type and WWOX-deficient neurons: the agonist against vehicle and against hormone-depleted medium, with a receptor-isoform-selective control; read precursor and mature-cell counts. Correction in both genotypes means non-specific maturation; correction only in the deficient condition opens a pre-onset in vivo question; no change closes the route.
feasibility: Development feasibility: a cell-level probe is feasible now, and an approved thyroid-hormone molecule and a clinical-stage analogue exist; systemic hormone action, the early treatment window and the lack of a brain-exposure datum for the analogue limit any later use.
novelty_perimeter: Queried: a whole-word name search of this module and its registries on 2026-11-03 (no hit for either molecule) and the compound-to-WWOX path of IT21 P3b. A name search in this module, not a statement about the literature.

intervention: HSC70 (HSPA8) inhibitor peptide forigerimod, with lysosomal and genetic controls
question: Is a destabilised Q230P-class WWOX missense protein cleared by an HSC70-linked lysosomal step in neural cells, and when that step is blocked does the spared protein regain GSK3B-docking function?
why_now: It is the only broad-recovery path found in IT21, and it depends on the allele: the chase and knockdown test either closes the route or turns a detectable-protein result into a function question. It enters at rank 6 on that ground, below the ten-row line, behind the premise measurements and behind the two rows that carry a risk flag or human clinical reports, not on novelty; the compound is not a development candidate.
evidence_available: WWOX-system: the Q230P class shows no protein band with a normal transcript; a different missense (P252A) over-expressed in non-neural cells is cleared faster and restored by lysosomal inhibitors but not by a proteasome inhibitor. Compound side: a curated inhibitor action on HSPA8 exists; the one reference reports impaired HSC70 refolding and lower lysosomal degradation in lupus-mouse B cells (abstract-level reading). Nothing shows that the route and the allele are the same. IT22 P6: the peptide's measured binding is micromolar (7.32 uM by surface plasmon resonance), refolding is inhibited at 40 uM, and its own paper reads its action as flux slowing like a lysosomal-acidification inhibitor; the one measured rescue of a WWOX missense is over-expressed P252A in non-neural cells.
decisive_uncertainty: Whether the same step clears the Q230P-class protein in neural cells, and whether spared protein is functional (the degron and the GSK3B docking site may be one conformational event, giving a stable but inert protein). HSC70 also folds proteins, so blocking it may harm instead of help; the mirrored harm arm is carried as a second conditional arm. IT22: the weakest link is the substrate itself: no WWOX missense protein is shown above the assay floor, so gate 0 is a KO-controlled blot for the protein (the G372R line first).
next_test: Chase of the Q230P-class protein with HSPA8 and LAMP2 knockdown and a lysosomal-acidification inhibitor, then a docking-function read (phospho-tau, with the L404A docking mutant as control). No rise with knockdown closes the route; a rise without function closes deep recovery on this route; both rising earns a variant-specific preclinical question, still not qualified. IT22: one cycloheximide-chase design with HSPA8 and LAMP2A knockdown and a lysosomal-acidification inhibitor tests every stability lever; the peptide is one arm, not the lead.

question: What does the published symptomatic response predict, and what does it not predict, about developmental outcome?
why_now: This is the thread with real human reports behind it and the one most likely to be read as a recommendation. The module already holds a series in which symptomatic response and developmental outcome did not move together, so the useful investigation is the separation itself, not another symptomatic observation.
evidence_available: Clinical reports only. Children counted once across 14 reports: 36 to 38 exposed to at least one of vigabatrin, hormonal therapy, ketogenic diet or cannabidiol (partial full-text depth in 11 reports, one source at abstract level). Both a symptomatic and a developmental outcome are recorded for 6. In 4 of them, a partial or transient improvement came with development unchanged; in 2, neither moved. No sustained, instrumented response is recorded, and no developmental gain follows any of the four classes. Vigabatrin: 5 children with both endpoints in 4 reports (4 discordant, 1 concordant non-response); these are not independent of the other classes, since three of the five also supply them and all five were on co-therapy. Children with both endpoints, by class, of those exposed: hormonal 3 of 11; ketogenic diet 2 of 12; cannabidiol 1 of 7. Counts only, no percentage (n below 10). Developmental statements are clinical narratives without a scale. A brain-imaging safety signal is recorded beside them in two children (abstract level, a report selected for the finding), so it is not a frequency. No WWOX child is recorded with a developmental gain after a symptomatic improvement. Four children in three reports (two of them in one report) had a partial, transient or clinically-defined improvement with development not progressing; two had neither. That is what the baseline in other genetic and structural early-onset encephalopathies predicts (a responder with poor development is the majority outcome in infantile spasms and near-universal in genetic strata), so it is not by itself a WWOX-specific feature. The comparison holds only as a binary: the baseline uses standardised scores with a cut, every WWOX developmental statement is a clinician narrative, and no WWOX child had a sustained, instrumented response. Non-WWOX DEE baseline (batch_sci_20261105 a2_baseline; not WWOX evidence): in a prospective IESS cohort read at partial full-text depth, 72 percent of responders (126 of 175, computed from its Table 1) were below the developmental cut at 3 years, and no genetic-aetiology child reached a favourable outcome (0 of 49, a count over all genetic-aetiology children, not a responder rate). In two randomised IESS trials (abstract level), arms that raised early spasm cessation by 15 to 19 points showed no demonstrated developmental difference, with about one chance in four of detecting the difference that full mediation would predict. In TSC, two randomised trials of pre-onset prevention changed seizure endpoints without changing development to 36 months; they test prevention before onset, not response after onset. The person-level association (ICISS, abstract level: 15.9 VABS points higher with early cessation) is carried by unknown aetiology and a normal first neurological examination.
decisive_uncertainty: Whether the separation of symptomatic response and development seen in WWOX-DEE cases differs from the base rate of genetic and structural DEEs, in which a responder with poor development is the expected case (in unknown aetiology the two are coupled, so the base rate does not extend to DEE generally); whether any WWOX-DEE case shows a change on a continuous developmental measure after a symptomatic response; whether a sustained response, which no published child achieved, is followed by gain; and whether the separation holds for residual-function alleles. The earlier contradiction with the mechanism argument is not unexplained: other genetic DEE cohorts (STXBP1, Dravet, KCNQ2; partial full-text and abstract depth, not WWOX evidence) report a developmental component independent of seizure control.
next_test: EXECUTED 2026-11-05: the published same-genotype cases with both a symptomatic and a developmental endpoint were assembled (6 children with both endpoints; a discordance rate is not computable at n below 10, so counts are given instead). Vigabatrin fired the 5-or-more branch (counts with sources); hormonal therapy, diet and cannabidiol fired the fewer-than-5 branch (not computable from the public record). Next: read these counts against the stratum base rates in a2_baseline/README.md section 1.3; only a WWOX-DEE responder rate with a favourable or improving developmental course clearly above the genetic-DEE base rate would be a WWOX finding. Denominator request, without contact: for each WWOX-DEE series that reports an intervention, the number exposed, the response definition, and a dated developmental instrument before and after a sustained response; where a source gives one, compare within-child continuous scores, since a cut at 70 cannot discriminate. The five-patient series and Choi 2026 come first, and the seven-child series (PMID 42721537) is read when an open route exists. No new exposure is proposed.

intervention: No compound: measurement of the parvalbumin interneuron population in neuron-targeted Wwox deletion, with cell number, identity and maturation, marker expression, intrinsic properties, synaptic input and circuit function read as six separate questions
question: In the neuron-targeted Wwox-deletion mouse, is the lower Pvalb transcript due to fewer parvalbumin interneurons, to immature or altered identity, to lower marker expression in a normal number of cells, to changed intrinsic properties, to less synaptic input onto or from them, or to a circuit-level change, and which of these is measured per animal?
why_now: It decides whether any parvalbumin-directed pharmacology, positive modulation or another kind, can be thought about at all, and which of the inhibitory-hypofunction contrasts to run first. Its direction is not assumed: raising parvalbumin-cell activity is not taken to be the right direction. It enters at rank 6 as a premise measurement because the nucleus-level route was closed by the replicate structure of the deposit and what remains is a per-animal measurement.
evidence_available: WWOX-system, transcript: a lower Pvalb transcript in the neuron-targeted deletion in bulk hippocampus (log2 -1.70, GSE158681 S contrast, as quoted in IT13b) and about half that size in the nuclear data (GSE158684: Pvalb 70 against 37 UMI in 3182 against 2920 nuclei; nuclei Pvalb share ratio 0.59). GSE158684 holds one pooled library per arm (library and animal index absent; the paper states n = 1 per arm), so nuclei are not biological replicates and the GSM records of the series are not independent experiments; PV-class nuclei number 12 to 19 per arm under the producer rules, the independent recompute disagrees on the specific counts, and PV composition and Pvalb per cell are undecidable under every rule tried. Kcnc1 is lower in inhibitory nuclei (one pool, not a replicate result). Immature-neuron markers (Sox11, Dcx, Igfbpl1) are higher in knockout neurons in direction; the larger composition change is oligodendrocyte-class nuclei, about 3- to 5-fold fewer. Wwox also falls in glia-called nuclei, unexplained. Protein and function, from the need file: PV-positive counts reduced by 44 percent in the whole hippocampus of a systemic constitutive knockout (PMID 30290271) and spontaneous inhibitory current amplitude more than halved in layer II/III pyramidal neurons of the neuron-specific knockout (PMID 34634460; pooled events, not animals). Raw reads of the eight snRNA experiments (SRX9206272 to SRX9206279) carried NCBI status hup on 2026-10-31. A public conference abstract (poster 014, Curing the Epilepsies 2026 programme, NINDS; the whole abstract was read, abstract level) describes a programme that combines genetic mouse models, in vivo electrophysiology, ex vivo slice recordings, cell type-specific manipulations and targeted pharmacological modulation of neuronal activity in WWOX deficiency, and names parvalbumin interneurons as the population of interest; it reports no quantitative result, no molecule, no rescue and no target. IT33 reading of the glial signal (NB-4 pilot, independently audited): the deletion is neuron-targeted by design (Synapsin-Cre) and a lower Wwox transcript also appears in glia-annotated nuclei of one pool (oligodendrocyte-called 193 to 1 UMI, astrocyte-called 156 to 9: very small counts on the deleted side, one pool per arm, so a count of cells or a statement of glial loss is not supported); the readings are several and not exclusive (lower transcript in the annotated class, class definition and detectability, ambient RNA, recombination beyond the expected cells, a change of state or composition), and none is isolated. Two abstract-level sources describe the Synapsin-Cre line: germline recombination through male carriers (PMID 16419044) and non-cell-autonomous astrogliosis after a neuronal deletion of another gene (PMID 11297510); neither shows or excludes recombination in glia or in parvalbumin cells of this deletion. IT33 verified delta (independent audit, 19 of 21 rows supported, two narrowed): an independent characterisation of the same Cre line with an X-linked Mecp2 reporter in adult male mice (PMID 35966957, full text without the figures) found reporter activation in 36 percent of NeuN-high brain nuclei, incomplete in cortex and minimal in cerebellum, and could not exclude activity in a subset of glia; the reporter, locus, age and cross differ from the Wwox deletion, so these percentages are not carried to the excision of Wwox or to parvalbumin cells; in the Wwox paper's P17 cortical field WWOX is retained in some NeuN-positive cells, and in one callosal field in some CC1-positive cells of the knockout; no tdTomato panel was found in the surfaces read.
decisive_uncertainty: Which of the six layers moves, per animal. A lower transcript does not show fewer cells, lower activity or less inhibition; an absent change in GSE158684 is not evidence of no change; the oligodendrocyte-lineage shift could be consequence or cause of an excitation-inhibition change and the data cannot say which. Whether any parvalbumin-cell change is a deficit, a compensation or a delayed maturation is unresolved, so the need direction stays unresolved and no lever sign is derived. Whether recombination reaches parvalbumin cells, and glia, in this deletion is not known from any source read, and a reporter measured in another context does not measure the excision of Wwox in parvalbumin cells.
next_test: Per-animal parvalbumin cell counts by immunostaining in neuron-targeted Wwox deletion against Cre-only controls, at least 3 animals per arm (reopening condition (c) of NP3A1), read together with a maturation and identity marker panel in the same animals, and, where the data holders allow, intrinsic-property and inhibitory-input recordings from labelled parvalbumin cells and a circuit-level read. Alternatives that also reopen it: a deposited library or animal index for GSE158684, or an independent neuron-targeted deletion dataset with at least 3 animals per arm and a parvalbumin-enriched capture. The result is read as six separate rows (number, identity and maturation, marker expression, intrinsic properties, synaptic input, circuit function); a change in one is not carried to another. In every animal used (P14 to P17, matching the phenotype window), on the same sections: a parvalbumin marker, the Rosa26 tdTomato reporter and a Wwox read-out, reporting per animal the fraction of parvalbumin cells reporter-positive, the fraction Wwox-negative and their concordance, beside cell number, identity and marker expression; transcript, protein, activity, cell number and circuit function stay separate results.

intervention: Class IIa-selective tool compound X against HDAC5 knockdown, with catalytic-dead and localisation-mutant HDAC5 rescue, a class-I-only inhibitor and an HDAC6 inhibitor as controls, in human neural cells
question: In human neural progenitors or neurons, does catalytic inhibition of class IIa HDACs lower the output of HDAC5 at SLC2A1 the way HDAC5 knockdown does, or does it leave it unchanged or raise it?
why_now: The HDAC5 to SLC2A1 thread rests on one muscle knockdown observation and has been carried as a limit, not a veto; the premise measurement it needs is the one open step of the IT28 challenge (WO-30). It sits at rank 7 because no neural line with the constructs is held and the readout does not change another row today.
evidence_available: Edge: HDAC5 to SLC2A1 traces to one origin, human primary muscle cells, where HDAC5 knockdown reduced GLUT1 expression (PMID 22991226, abstract level); the one drug tested there was pan-HDAC and was reported for GLUT4 only. Class IIa enzymes have very low intrinsic activity on standard substrates and repress largely as scaffolds; in neurons the separating experiments exist for HDAC4, not HDAC5; cardiomyocyte data show catalytic activity mattering for HDAC5 with the opposite sign (inhibition raises the output). Compound side: Compound X identity confirmed by full InChIKey (CHEMBL3110004); ChEMBL values from one paper, HDAC4 130, HDAC5 80, HDAC7 40, HDAC9 20 nM, in a recombinant catalytic-domain assay, cross-paper values vary and whether each was measured or quoted was not checked; whether compound X engages HDAC5 in cells at the cited exposures is not determined. Attribution gap of the pan-class comparator in this thread: vorinostat is held on main_target_weak_attribution (HDAC5 Ki 3600 against HDAC1 1.3 nM, fold 2769.2), so an effect of that compound would read as class I. Counter-premise carried in the generator: class I and pan-HDAC inhibition are signed adverse for oligodendrocyte maturation; for class IIa the CNS sign is unknown, the only myelin datum is a peripheral Schwann-cell double mutant of Hdac4 and Hdac5 (PMID 29472387, partial full text), and WWOX neuron-deleted mice are hypomyelinated. WWOX-system: HDAC5 mRNA nominally lower and SLC2A1 nominally higher in the P47T mouse, an mRNA association only; the human organoid shows SLC2A1 higher on transcript. IT32 reading of neural precedents: a catalytic-domain mutant of HDAC5 (two cysteines) lost deacetylase activity in vitro and abolished the effect of nuclear HDAC5 on one transcript and on a behaviour in rat nucleus accumbens (PMID 39923817, full text; no SLC2A1 or glucose readout, and loss of binding to another factor is not excluded), so the earlier statement that no neural catalytic arm exists is out of date; a catalytic-site mutant of the paralog HDAC4 rescued survival like the wild type in mouse cortical neurons (PMID 23141539); an inhibitor matched knockdown on neurite growth in neural cells but was inert where knockdown of HDAC7 acted (PMID 31572723; PMID 41962726, abstract only). Catalytic dependence is therefore specific to paralog, cell type and output. IT32 action-level reading (NB-3b): the premise source tested knockdown only, that is protein amount, and its pan-inhibitor arm names no GLUT1 result (abstract level); results for the paralog HDAC4 on GLUT1 go in both directions in non-neural cells; the direction of SLC2A1 in WWOX-deficient systems differs between the organoid, mouse brain and shWWOX neural cells, and no source reads SLC2A1 after HDAC5 manipulation in a neural cell.
decisive_uncertainty: Whether catalytic inhibition reproduces knockdown at SLC2A1 in a human neural cell: knockdown is not catalytic inhibition when the enzyme acts mostly as a scaffold. The premise is refuted if a catalytic-dead rescue restores SLC2A1 like wild type, if compound X leaves SLC2A1 unchanged while knockdown moves it and its cellular engagement of HDAC5 has been shown (without that, a null cannot separate scaffold function from non-engagement); a class-I-only inhibitor that reproduces the knockdown is ambiguous, because HDAC5 repression runs through HDAC3, and does not refute it alone; if inhibition raises SLC2A1 the lever inverts. Whether a change in SLC2A1 is favourable, compensatory or harmful in WWOX-deficient neural cells is itself unresolved, and a change in SLC2A1 is not a benefit. Potency of the broader HDAC compounds on HDAC5 cannot be compared until the methods of the three potency papers are readable (WO-29, data access blocked).
next_test: Step 1, no compound: HDAC5 knockdown in human neural progenitors or neurons reading SLC2A1 protein, glucose uptake and transcript, with rescue by wild type, a localisation mutant and a catalytic-site mutant. Step 2, only after cellular engagement of endogenous HDAC5 by the compound is shown with a readout specific to it (bulk histone acetylation is a weak reading for a class IIa enzyme): compound X, a class-I-only inhibitor (an ambiguous comparator) and an HDAC6 inhibitor as a chemotype comparator that needs its own qualification, not as a negative control. A myelin-relevant readout (oligodendrocyte-precursor differentiation, with and without neuron conditioning) is proposed in the IT29 P10 question record for the same experiment.
feasibility: Wet-lab measurement; no neural line with the constructs is held in the module. As a drug question, no statement of CNS exposure of the compounds is carried here. A compound result on this row would be read as a premise result, never as evidence that any compound works.

A search of this module, not a statement about the literature. The vorinostat thread is an already-known internal reference, not an independent source of support.

intervention: No compound: measurement of the role of the MYC rise in WWOX-deficient radial glia
question: Is the MYC rise in WWOX-deficient radial glia a driver of the progenitor shift, a marker of a retained progenitor state, or a consequence of the cell-cycle shift?
why_now: 555 of the 994 generated proposals end in a change of MYC, 314 in a harm arm and 241 in a protect arm (123 eligible for hand-over); whether any change of MYC is wanted depends on this role, so one measurement stands behind all of them and no MYC-directed lever is assumed beneficial.
evidence_available: WWOX-system, one organoid study (PMID 42397075): MYC is the most raised gene in knockout radial glia, which shift toward S and G2M; the fraction of SOX2-positive cells that are MYC-positive is raised in an engineered knockout and two patient-derived lines; one non-selective multi-kinase inhibitor reported to suppress Wnt and MYC lowers the SOX2-positive fraction in knockout organoids; neuron-promoter add-back raises deep-layer fractions. Transcript and cell fractions only: no protein, no manipulation of MYC itself.
decisive_uncertainty: Driver, marker or consequence. If the MYC difference vanishes within cell-cycle and potency strata it is a marker and this observation alone justifies no lever; if genetic lowering of MYC moves the progenitor shift it is a driver, and the timing of any window is a separate question, not assumed to be prenatal only. MYC dose is two-sided in cortex and the record holds no safe pharmacological formulation for a developing compartment.
next_test: In WWOX-deficient and corrected isogenic organoids or radial-glia cultures: compare MYC within cell-cycle phase strata, then lower MYC by a genetic route with a second construct and read the progenitor fractions and the cell-cycle phase. No compound is needed for this step.
feasibility: Existing organoid systems; wet-lab measurement, not executable from this module.
novelty_perimeter: Queried on 2026-11-07: the MYC need record, work-order entry WO-33, map row WO-33 and the stage S12 proposal table; a search of this module, not a statement about the literature. A scientific package on this role (NB-1) was in progress and is not used here.

intervention: Ih (HCN) channel blockers of at least two chemotypes as a tool arm in Wwox-deficient cortical slices, read with sag, resting potential and burst incidence in the same slices
question: In Wwox-deficient layer II/III slices, does blocking Ih lower burst incidence, raise it, or leave it unchanged, when sag, resting potential and input resistance are read in the same cells?
why_now: The module holds a graded sag, a depolarised resting potential and a larger rebound with no consumer, and the heterozygote shows the same intrinsic changes yet rarely bursts. Three readings give opposite signs for the same drug class, so no Ih-directed compound can be ranked until one measurement separates them.
evidence_available: WWOX-system, one preparation read in full and re-extracted (PMID 34634460, Table 1 and Figure 6): resting potential -79.25, -75.51, -73.62 mV and sag 1.18, 2.04, 2.57 mV grade with gene dose, input resistance saturates at one allele, rebound is larger only in the knockout, and bursts occur in 36 of 42 knockout, 4 of 23 heterozygote and 0 of 11 wild-type slices; the authors attribute the hyperexcitability to the depolarised resting potential and cite discordant Ih-blocker precedents, including worsening of 4-AP events. Compound side: Ih-acting tools exist in the catalogue (a clinically used HCN blocker and several research blockers, identities resolved), found by the need search without naming any; their cellular potency in a cortical pyramidal neuron and their selectivity among HCN isoforms were not assessed here. No Ih-blocker experiment in a Wwox-deficient preparation is recorded in the entries read.
decisive_uncertainty: Branch A, compensatory Ih: blocking it worsens or leaves bursts; weakened if bursts fall. Branch B, pro-excitatory Ih through the depolarised resting potential: blocking it lowers bursts at matched membrane potential; weakened if bursts do not fall. Branch C, bystander: no effect on bursts although sag falls; weakened by any burst change. The sag itself must first be shown to be Ih (sensitive to the blocker), and a blocker that shifts the resting potential acts on the premises of A and B at once.
next_test: In knockout, heterozygote and wild-type slices: sag, resting potential, input resistance, rebound and burst incidence before and after two Ih blockers of different chemotypes (the second so that an off-target action is not read as Ih), with a current-clamp step that matches the resting potential, and a voltage-clamp read of the blocker-sensitive current in a subset of cells; animals, not cells, are the replicates.
feasibility: Ex vivo slice electrophysiology in an existing Wwox neuron-deleted line; tool compounds only; no brain-exposure statement is carried here and none is implied for any clinically used member.
novelty_perimeter: Queried on 2026-11-07: the needs table (no HCN target in any need before this one), the IT14 P3 package, the investigations table, the stage proposals S12 and S13 (no HCN main target or chain) and the catalogue by target and by id; a search of this module, not a statement about the literature.

evidence_solidity: Conditional hypothesis: the observations are verified, the sign of the intervention is open in all three branches, and no Ih-blocker experiment exists in the system.
movement_note: New row, enters at rank 7 below the ten-row line. Reasons: it turns an observation that no consumer used into a discriminating tool experiment with three opposite-sign branches. Not rewarded: novelty.
